claims.text: A composite integrating layered MoS2 into a high-strength metal or ceramic matrix can provide self-lubrication across a wide temperature range.
Such a composite can maintain mechanical integrity across a wide temperature range.
The proposed material contains a high-strength matrix with a dispersed layered transition-metal-dichalcogenide lubricating phase such as MoS2.
MoS2 should be uniformly distributed in the matrix during composite synthesis.
The proposed composite is intended to operate under sliding contact from ambient temperature to approximately 600°C.
The layered structure of MoS2 facilitates easy shear.
The matrix provides a reinforcement effect in the composite.
At lower temperatures, sliding between MoS2 layers provides lubrication.
At higher temperatures, the composite matrix supports the structure.
At higher temperatures, the matrix preserves the integrity of the MoS2 lubricating phase.
The combination of MoS2 lubrication and matrix support balances mechanical strength with friction reduction.
The proposed composite will exhibit stable friction coefficients over a broad temperature range.
The proposed composite will exhibit low wear rates over a broad temperature range.
The proposed composite will maintain mechanical strength over a broad temperature range.
The matrix without a solid-lubricant phase typically has inferior lubrication performance at high temperatures.
An excessively high MoS2 concentration may significantly degrade mechanical strength.
Inadequate bonding between MoS2 and the matrix may prevent the proposed behavior at extreme temperatures.
